jurisdiction.venue: Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Gurugram Zonal Office (PMLA, 2002)

headline: E.D. Attaches ₹545.96 Crore in Vatika Group Assets, Including Mehrauli Farmhouse, Over Alleged Double-Sold Gurugram Plots
deck: Fourteen years after upfront payments yielded zero plots in Vatika India Next-2, investigators allege promoters Anil and Gautam Bhalla—in judicial custody since September—resold 66 plots already contracted to a ₹473 crore buyer.

financials.prison_display: Pending (Anil & Gautam Bhalla in Judicial Custody)

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: India’s Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached ₹545.96 crore in Vatika Group and Bhalla family-trust properties—quantifying ₹568 crore (~$66.8M) in alleged proceeds—over accusations of 14-year plot non-delivery, 22 employee-less land-bank shells, and double-selling 66 already-sold Gurugram plots.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Collecting full upfront payment for the same residential lot twice from two different buyers without telling either one, while keeping the original purchaser waiting fourteen years for an empty deed
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Up to seven years’ rigorous imprisonment under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act upon conviction; both detained promoters remain presumed innocent

sources.title: Press Release on the Provisional Attachment Order of Vatika Group & Its Promoters in a Money Laundering Case

interactive_art_spec.caption: Gurugram’s commercial and residential skyline in Haryana. The Enforcement Directorate’s Gurugram Zonal Office provisionally attached ₹545.96 crore in Vatika Group and Bhalla family-trust real estate, including a Sultanpur Farms property in Mehrauli, New Delhi.
